newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton, Yeltsin pledge to minimise NATO problems.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin pledge to minimise NATO problems.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin promised on Friday to try to avoid problems caused by disagreements over NATO enlargement by boosting ties between the alliance and Moscow.
The pledge to avoid trouble came in a statement issued by the two leaders at the end of their summmit, during which Yeltsin repeated Moscow's stiff opposition to NATO's expansion plans.
"They continued to disagree on the issue of NATO enlargement," the statement said.

"In order to minimise the potential consequences of this disagreement the presidents agreed that they should work, both together and with others, on a document that will establish cooperation between NATO and Russia as an important element of a new comprehensive European security system..."
NATO is already negotiating the terms of a new partnership with Russia which will give Moscow a voice in European security affairs without giving it a veto over alliance decisions.
